activity.title: There's no better place to explore the future of artificial intelligence than San Francisco. Every conversation brings new ideas, new perspectives, and new opportunities to learn from the people building the next generation of AI. Our CEO, Ed Van Deman, recently attended an AI conference alongside the newest member of the Forest team, our AI Summer Intern, Murtaza. It was a great opportunity to connect with innovators, exchange ideas, and stay at the forefront of the rapidly evolving AI landscape. As Forest AI continues to grow, experiences like these help shape how we bring practical, secure AI capabilities directly into financial workflows. From learning about emerging technologies to building relationships within the AI community, we are committed to developing solutions that deliver real value for family offices, wealth managers, and financial organizations. We're excited to have Murtaza on the team this summer and look forward to the contributions he will make as we continue expanding Forest AI. The future of AI is being built through collaboration, and we're excited to be part of the journey. #ArtificialIntelligence #GenerativeAI #FamilyOffice #WealthManagement #Accounting #FinancialTechnology #MachineLearning #DataSecurity #SOC2 #ForestSystems ...more ...more

This weekend with the help of my friends, I worked on training a local vision-language-action model (SmolVLA) model to drive a rover autonomously. It is trained on demonstrations generated in a MuJoCo sim; scored on a HUD leaderboard that proves the learned policy beats random / scripted-expert baselines. The judged artifact (P0) needs no working rover. The learned policy does surprisingly well for a small local model that has ~450 million parameters. Though the gap between sim and real is big. I have open sourced the trained model and it is available on HuggingFace for those who would be interested on further training it on real-world data. demo: https://lnkd.in/gqjqG_QE ...more

I’m excited to share a follow up to my previous project artki dot tech: Gaudí! In the updated version, you can draw a 2D floor plan in the browser, click build, and walk through the 3D model of the house designed. The biggest update in this version is moving from uploading a static floor plan to a dynamic one where you can draw and decor the interiors of your house. I am glad to share that I accepted an offer from ALPhA (Algorithms for Learning Physics Applications) to do research under the mentorship of Dr. Raghuram Ramanujan and Dr. Michelle Kuchera . In my research, I will focus on applying machine learning techniques to fundamental nuclear physics applications. This is an invaluable opportunity for me, since I have always been passionate about applying machine learning in scientific research, and this summer I will have the chance to finally do it. I am grateful to Dr. Ramanujan and Dr. Kuchera for providing me with this opportunity and I am excited to work alongside other distinguished researchers. ...more

Yesterday, standing in front of a room full of investors in Arlington, I pitched AidOS — and I and Aseel walked out with the B Ventures SAFE investment as the winner of the inaugural PeaceTech Accelerator Demo Day cohort. 🕊️ I am still processing what this means and how this feels. Two months ago, six founders walked into the first cohort of the PeaceTech Accelerator, an experiment one mile from the Pentagon built on a premise: that peace is a market, and that founders building technology to reduce violent conflict deserve the same effort, capital, and go-to-market machinery as any defense tech company. To Shane Ray Martin and @Brian Adams — thank you for betting on us. To our partners and sponsors — @Salesforce, @Carta, @Rho, @FinStrat, @Arlington Economic Development, — thank you for two months of providing advice, sharpened messaging, sharper pipelines, and warm introductions that will outlast this program. To the founders in our cohort — we came in as strangers and left as a network. I learned from every one of you. I won't lie: I was nervous walking on stage. But somewhere between the practice reps and the third version of the pitch, the message was clear. AidOS isn't a nice-to-have. It is the operating system for a new humanitarian aid architecture. We are building the infrastructure for decentralized, verifiable, community-led aid — powered by a unique digital identity, a local hero's network for last-mile delivery, and Buy Good for economic dignity. Today, 3,500+ agents across all 34 provinces of Afghanistan and Gaza, already run on this rail. Tomorrow, it powers response in Syria, Sudan, Yemen and across Africa. The peace sector has been told for decades that it isn't investable and yesterday we provided otherwise. To the investors, funders, and operators in my network: if you believe humanitarian infrastructure is a category — not a charity line item — I want to talk to you. This is a $30B+ market moving toward decentralization, and we are building the layer it runs on. Send me a DM. Let's make time to create meaningful, purposeful and profitable good tech that works for everyone.

Excited to share that I've started a new role as a Data Analyst with the Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (CSTAR) at NYU Langone Health . I'll be working on optimization and simulation research to help inform transplant policy and improve organ allocation systems. This marks the beginning of my career after graduating from Davidson College , where I studied Computer Science. I'm incredibly grateful to my family, mentors, professors, and friends for their support throughout this journey. I'm excited to join a team whose work has a direct impact on people's lives and to begin this next chapter in New York City.
